One fly per cell: seat each fly on the rim or open lid of its own cell, pin each pill just outside its cell with a short leader, never over a fly.

Make the kept wild female the hero: raise the keep bulb off the footer, scale her up with a rim light inside the gold band, recolour the beetle away from warm orange.

Finish the trap and clear the type: weathered polymer with grime, a moulded funnel cone, camera closer and lower, limb and flies out of the type column, mesquite silhouettes instead of acacias.

Make the plan the hero: a raised fan of release swaths in translucent resin over the relief starting at Edinburg, unevenly spaced so it reads as chosen, led back to Kerrville by one engraved channel. No count, illustrative, never dusk gold.
If the dividers stay, finish them as an object with each tip under its pill, and remove the darker slab with a straight edge in the upper left.

Give the forty a subject only this story has, without drawing a trap: the chosen unit carries the deck's second door that the other 39 lack, abstract, or the units become release boxes or fly stations.
Push in and drop the camera so the 40 fill the upper two thirds, press an empty slot with a drag track to the forward unit, and move away from frame 8's golden stubble and fence world.
Show all 19 posts in frame and end the fence at a marked last post where the road runs on.
Move away from slide 7's world: a worm's eye down the post line or a blue hour sky with no honey ground, and rebuild the foreground grass cards.

Drop the fence and grass plane shared with frame 8, push in to the hands and phone, and fix the mannequin hands, hair, hat and shirt.
